Claude Buddy no longer dies overnight while your screen is locked. That is this release.

0.5.4-beta shipped a few hours ago and cleared a week of backlog. This one is small and deliberate: five pull requests, one of which fixes a crash that had been in the app since at least 7 September, and four of which make the test suite tell the truth about itself.

Still a beta. The crash fix was measured against the real failure on a real Mac; what was and was not verified is in *Known limitations*.

## Fixed: the app started into a locked screen and aborted

If Claude Buddy launched while your screen was locked — a login item on a machine you had walked away from, or a keep-alive restart overnight — it waited for the screen to unlock, gave up after two hours, and then **started anyway into a screen that was still locked**. CoreVideo refused, nothing caught it, and the process died. On a machine left locked overnight it would die and stay dead until somebody came back and noticed.

The wait function had the answer the whole time. It returned a `bool` meaning "the cap expired and the screen is *still* locked", and the code that called it took that as an `Action` — so the answer was discarded by the signature, silently, and the app started regardless.

It now distinguishes three states rather than two. The window server saying nothing at all is genuine ignorance and still bounded. The window server saying the screen is unlocked starts immediately, as before. The window server saying the screen is **locked** now waits — up to twelve hours rather than two, because in that state the app demonstrably cannot draw, and the alternative to waiting is a crash.

Twelve hours is a bound rather than an absence of one, and that is the deliberate part. If the lock signal were ever wrong, an uncapped wait would mean the app is simply never there, with no menu-bar icon and no way in — and this project would rather have a crash it can recover from than a silence it cannot. An expired bound starts the app; if the screen really was locked, the crash restarts under the keep-alive and tries again.

## Fixed: the test suite told the truth about itself

Four changes with no user-visible effect, kept together because they are one story.

Two tests failed intermittently on loaded machines — one racing a five-millisecond timer against its own teardown, one racing another test class for a shared directory. The second turned out to be reachable three calls deep from any test that refuses a persona picture, which is why three separate attempts to fix it by listing the classes involved each found one more class the last had missed.

It is now fixed structurally instead: a test's scratch log directory has no process-wide name at all, so a test that forgets to isolate cannot reach another's. A guard pins that to a single read site so it stays true. And a side effect nobody had filed — test runs writing entries into the real `~/Library/Logs/ClaudeBuddy` — stops too, which matters the next time somebody reads that file to diagnose a genuine crash.

One claim in this repository's own contributor documentation was also wrong and is corrected: a background job does get a window server session, contrary to what the file had said for months, and an arm of the crash fix had been justified on that.

## Known limitations

The locked-screen path was verified by reading the state off a second Mac that was genuinely locked, over SSH, rather than by locking the machine under test — so the behaviour is measured, not inferred. The crash itself was reproduced from its own crash log and system power log.

Not verified: that this specific crash on 22 September took the locked branch rather than the unknown one. After the fix both branches are correct and the crash is prevented either way, so the question no longer decides anything — but the causal claim is narrower than "we know exactly what happened", and it is stated that way.

Windows is unaffected by the crash fix, which is macOS-only by construction, and was not driven by hand. Both platforms run the full suite in CI.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.5-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.5-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.5-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

## Upgrading

Replace the app as usual. On macOS, replacing `/Applications/Claude Buddy.app` gives the bundle a new code identity, so the Automation and Local Network permissions are re-evaluated against it — if click-to-focus or anything on your LAN stops working after an upgrade, that is where to look first.
